hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes training into divergence, so accuracy drops far more than at low or mid rates.
At very small learning rates the network is under-trained in 243 epochs, so a larger step helps much more than elsewhere.
With a tiny learning rate, a larger batch means fewer updates and even more under-training.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilise training that is unstable at high learning rates.
Large batches give few updates per epoch, so a higher learning rate compensates and helps more than with small batches.
Small batches are noisy and make many updates, so a higher learning rate becomes unstable sooner.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty over-regularizes the model and hurts accuracy, unlike at negligible alpha.
Deeper networks are more prone to instability and dead ReLUs at high learning rates.
Wider layers produce larger effective updates, so they diverge more readily at high learning rates.
Smaller batches add gradient noise, which compounds with a high learning rate and degrades accuracy.
